items.title: Agents now manage Gemini compute
items.oneliner: DeepMind says AI agents now allocate some Gemini compute, which makes closed-loop experimentation operational, not theoretical.

items.title: OpenAI is tightening usage economics
items.oneliner: OpenAI warns heavy ChatGPT users will hit limits sooner, a clear sign inference costs are finally biting.

items.title: Google tightened Workspace agent rules
items.oneliner: Google's Workspace MCP terms add task-only processing and 30-day retention, which sharply narrows long-memory enterprise agents.

items.title: New York banned AI chatbot toys
items.oneliner: New York banned AI chatbot toys, giving consumer AI regulation another real enforcement edge beyond voluntary safety talk.

items.title: Ransomware recovery firm was indicted
items.oneliner: The CTO of RansomwareHelp was indicted after allegedly paying hackers secretly, exposing a grim supply chain inside cyber recovery.

items.title: A script targets data brokers
items.oneliner: A Python tool automates data-broker opt-outs, turning privacy cleanup from paperwork into something engineers can actually operationalize.

items.title: AMD got a faster llama.cpp fork
items.oneliner: An AMD-specific llama.cpp fork boosts token generation and prefill, reminding teams that inference is fragmenting by hardware.

items.title: PostgreSQL now fits one executable
items.oneliner: Minipg packages PostgreSQL into a single executable, which could simplify CI, local testing, and disposable data environments.

items.title: Three browser VMs run in-tab
items.oneliner: A browser tab now spins up Linux VMs for Chrome, Firefox, and Safari, making cross-browser debugging radically cheaper.

items.title: Rust gained a full VoIP stack
items.oneliner: Rvoip 0.5 ships SIP, RTP, WebRTC, and QUIC in Rust, lowering the barrier to build communications products in-house.
